title: Proposed Initiative Proposition Number One: Homeowner's Property Tax Exemption

context.text: Citizen initiative, "People's Initiative to Limit Property Tax in Wyoming through a Homeowner's Property Exemption." Secretary of State Chuck Gray certified it on January 2, 2025 after verifying 30,251 valid signatures, and described it as the first initiative on a Wyoming ballot in 30 years. Wyoming Public Media reports it was spearheaded by Brent Bien, Rich Weber and Cheryl Aguiar under the name BCR Initiatives and is endorsed by the Wyoming Republican Party; a coalition called Vote No on Prop 1 (including the Wyoming Education Association, Wyoming Hospital Association, Wyoming Association of Community College Trustees, Wyoming Taxpayers Association and Wyoming Realtors) opposes it.

question.text: Shall a law be enacted: Establishing a property tax exemption for qualified homeowners’ primary residence in the amount of fifty percent (50%) of the assessed value of the dwelling; AND Defining “homeowner” and “primary residence”; providing that no more than one exemption shall apply to a single property or be claimed by a single owner per year; requiring a homeowner to be a resident of Wyoming for at least one year and to have occupied the primary residence for at least six months of the previous tax year to qualify; requiring an initial sworn claim to be filed with the county assessor by the fourth Monday in May; providing for continuing the exemption in subsequent years through annually confirming eligibility; providing a penalty for false claims; clarifying that the exemption applies to the residential structure; and specifying applicability? Estimated Fiscal Impact: Anticipated Revenue / (decrease) Fiscal Year 2028 ($92,614,266) Fiscal Year 2029 ($95,855,766) The above estimate is based on residential property assessed value and property tax data from the Computer Assisted Mass Appraisal (CAMA) system provided by the Department of Revenue in 2023. The future fiscal impact estimates are derived by using the January 2023 Consensus Revenue Estimating Group (CREG) report, estimating annual growth of 3.5% for properties in the future years. This is an estimate of fiscal impact to the State of Wyoming only and does not include an estimate of any impact upon political subdivisions. The proposition references a beginning in 2025, but if passed in 2026 the earliest applicable tax year would be 2027, with impact to the state beginning in 2028. Fiscal impact will apply to each year so long as the exemption is in place. Future impacts depend on unpredictable economic conditions.

summary.text: The initiative would exempt from property taxation 50 percent of the assessed value of a qualifying homeowner's primary residence, one exemption per property and per owner per year. To qualify, the owner must have lived in Wyoming at least one year and in the residence at least six months of the prior tax year, file a sworn claim with the county assessor by the fourth Monday in May, and confirm eligibility annually; false claims are punishable under W.S. 6-5-303. Fiscal impact per the Secretary of State's ballot language: an anticipated state revenue decrease of $92,614,266 in fiscal year 2028 and $95,855,766 in fiscal year 2029, which the estimate says covers the State only and not political subdivisions. Wyoming Public Media reports a Department of Revenue analysis putting the decrease at up to $124.7 million annually, and that there is no income or age limit, the exemption applies to residential structures but not land, and the Legislature already provides a 25 percent exemption on the first $1 million of a home's value that a homeowner would have to choose between.

measure.yesMeans: Enacts a law exempting 50 percent of the assessed value of a qualified homeowner's primary residence from property taxation, on the terms in the ballot language ("FOR").
measure.noMeans: Does not enact the exemption; existing property tax law and exemptions stay as they are ("AGAINST").

argumentsFor.text: Bryan Miller, chairman of the Wyoming Republican Party, said when the party announced its support: "Wyoming homeowners deserve meaningful, durable property-tax relief, and our party is prepared to help communicate the case for this initiative to voters across the state."
Brent Bien, who led the initiative campaign, told Cowboy State Daily in September 2023: "If there's one thing this whole campaign is about is freedom."

argumentsAgainst.text: The Vote No on Prop 1 Committee's website states: "Prop 1 proposes a 50% cut in property taxes but has no plan for how to replace over $125 million in lost funding in year one."

Jerimiah Rieman, executive director of the Wyoming County Commissioners Association, said: "The strain that is going to be most painful is around those special districts that rely almost exclusively on property taxes to provide for fire, ambulance, hospital," per Wyoming Public Media.

researchNotes: Ballot language and fiscal estimate are verbatim from the Wyoming Secretary of State's 2026 Statewide Ballot Propositions document; the Laramie County sample ballot shows the same text and no other statewide proposition or constitutional amendment, and the Secretary of State's document lists only this one. Wyoming has no official argument pamphlet. For-side evidence is thinner than against-side: the second 'for' entry is a short 2023 sponsor quotation (no 2026 sponsor campaign statement or website was located); a news paraphrase of the sponsors' position was removed. The fiscal figure up to $124.7 million is a Department of Revenue analysis as reported by news, differing from the Secretary of State's State-only estimate.
